title: U.S. House · West Virginia's 2nd District
area: West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, covering the eastern panhandle and central/southern parts of the state including Charleston.

context.text: Incumbent Riley Moore (R) ran unopposed in the Republican primary. Ace Parsi won the Democratic primary on May 12, 2026.

summary.text: Riley Moore is the incumbent U.S. Representative for West Virginia's 2nd District, seeking re-election in 2026. He previously served as West Virginia State Treasurer.

background.text: Born in Morgantown, West Virginia; lives in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government and international politics from George Mason University and a master's degree in strategic security studies from the National Defense University.
Career experience includes working as a national security staffer for the U.S. House Committee on Foreign Affairs and as a contract employee for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.
Served as West Virginia State Treasurer before his election to the U.S. House in 2022.

positions.summary: In a 2025 op-ed he called for the largest deportation operation in American history and praised funding for expanded ICE detention capacity and more ICE agents.
positions.quote: President Trump needs to finish the wall and engage in the largest deportation operation in American history to undo the Biden border invasion.

positions.summary: After the Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under IEEPA, he criticized the ruling and introduced the U.S. Reciprocal Trade Act to authorize the President to impose reciprocal tariffs.
positions.quote: The Court’s decision to strike down President Trump’s tariff policy is egregiously wrong, both as a matter of law and as a matter of justice for American workers.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Appropriations for the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including as Vice Chair of the Legislative Branch subcommittee, and to the Commerce-Justice-Science and Labor-HHS-Education subcommittees.

summary.text: Ace Parsi is a public education and democracy advocate running as the Democratic nominee for West Virginia's 2nd District.

background.text: Immigrated to the United States at age eight and a half, having fled a dictatorship.
Earned a high school diploma from Wyoming Area High School and a bachelor's degree from Penn State University (2005).
Career experience includes working as an advocate on public education issues.

priorities.text: "We can have a more affordable future. By overturning the cuts in the Big Beautiful Bill, turning back tariffs on groceries, eliminating the current benefit cliffs... we can have that."
"We can have a more caring future. By investing in infrastructure around clean drinking water and investing in the individuals in care jobs whether they're nurses and teachers or law enforcement."

"We can have a more empowered future. We can take the power back from big tech and their AI imagined future and create systems and relationships where government and elected officials are more responsive."

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for ending the current tariffs and for Congress to exercise authority over them, while saying tariffs should be used to level the playing field.
positions.quote: Tariffs are taxes on consumers that have raised the prices for everything from ground beef to Christmas toys.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for pursuing a single-payer public option and reversing Medicaid cuts in the 2025 budget law.
positions.quote: Healthcare: Fund rural hospitals; pursue a single-payer public option

positions.summary: His campaign platform lists raising the minimum wage to a living wage.
positions.quote: Raise the minimum wage to a living wage

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for tax incentives and zoning reform to build more housing.
positions.quote: Housing: Tax incentives and zoning reform to build more housing so West Virginians can afford to stay in West Virginia

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for redirecting funds lost to vouchers back into public schools.
positions.quote: redirect lost funds for vouchers back into public schools

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for diversifying energy supply through wind, solar and other sources and for cutting fossil fuel subsidies.
positions.quote: Energy: Diversify supply through wind, solar, and other sources to drive down heating bills
